conversation.contentPreview:
Create a complete single self-contained file `chip8_ollama-qwen3.8-27b_01.html` (HTML + CSS + JavaScript inline;
no external libraries, CDNs, assets or backend). Build a working CHIP-8 emulator.

Implement the interpreter properly: 4 KB of memory with the font set loaded at 0x050 and programs at 0x200,
sixteen 8-bit registers V0 to VF, the 16-bit index register, the program counter, a call stack, and the
delay and sound timers counting down at 60 Hz. Decode and execute the complete instruction set of 35
instructions, including the arithmetic and logic group with the carry and borrow flags in VF, the shift
instructions, jumps and calls, the random instruction, BCD conversion, register save and load, and the key
tests.

The display is 64 by 32 pixels drawn on a canvas scaled to a readable size, with sprites drawn by XOR and
the collision flag set in VF. The 16-key keypad is mapped to a 4 by 4 block of keyboard keys shown in the
interface; key press and release must both reach the emulator.

Include a small demo ROM as a byte array inside the file: a real program, assembled by you, that draws a
sprite and moves or reacts to a key, so that the emulator can be tried without any download. Also allow
loading a ROM from a local file.

Add run, pause, single step and reset controls, an adjustable instructions-per-frame speed, and a debugger
panel showing the registers, the index register, the program counter, the stack and the decoded current
instruction. Every visible control must work. Deliver the one file `chip8_ollama-qwen3.8-27b_01.html`.

{"thought":"Bugs to fix in the created file:
1. Demo ROM: `A0 02 20` = LD I, 0x0220 — correct (I=0x220, sprite there). But `10 02 16` = JP 0x216 (0x20A+4=0x20E, +2=0x210, +2=0x212... wait let me recount addresses: 0x200: 60 0A, 0x202: 61 0A, 0x204: 62 01, 0x206: A0 02 20 (3 bytes? no, A0nnn is 2 bytes: A0 20... wait nnn=0x0220 so bytes are A0 20? No: A0nnn = 0xA000 | nnn = 0xA220, bytes: A2 20. So the ROM array has "0xA0, 0x0220" which is WRONG — 0x0220 is not a valid byte; it gets truncated to 0x20. So the instruction becomes A0 20 = LD I, 0x0020! Bug. Must be 0xA2, 0x20.
2. Similarly JP 0x216 → 0x1216 → bytes 12 16 (fine, 2 bytes: 0x12, 0x16). In the array I wrote "0x10, 0x216" — 0x216 truncated to 0x16 → instruction 0x1016 = JP 0x16! Bug. Same for "0x10, 0x20A" → 0x20A & 0xFF = 0x0A → JP 0x0A! Bug.
3. decode() for 0xAN has a typo: `(ins & 0x00F0) === 0x00AN` — 0x00AN is not valid JS (A-N? actually 0x00AN — 'A' is hex, 'N' is invalid → SyntaxError!). This breaks the whole script. Must fix to 0x00A0.
4. decode() 8NN7 line: `"V" + y", "V[x] = V[y] - V[x]"` — mismatched quote → SyntaxError. Must fix.
5. DRW: after drawing, spec says I unchanged; fine. But drawSprite sets V[0xF] even when setCollisionFlag is false? No — only when true. Good. However for DRW, spec: VF set to 1 if any set pixel would be erased. My XOR approach: collision if display bit was 1 before XOR. Correct.
6. The demo ROM as written (DEMO_FINAL) has the byte bugs above. Need to rewrite with proper byte pairs.
7. `0x10, 0x210` etc all truncated.
8. Also in DEMO_FINAL: after `E0 95` (SKP V5) at 0x208: if key pressed, skip 2 → lands at 0x20C... let me lay out: 0x206: A2 20 (LD I,0x220); 0x208: E0 95 (SKP V5); if pressed skip → pc=0x20C: 62 FF (LD V2, 0xFF); 0x20E: 12 16 (JP 0x216); 0x210: 12 16 (JP 0x216); 0x212: 80 22 (ADD V0,V2); 0x214: D0 04 (DRW V0,V1,4); 0x216: 12 0A (JP 0x20A)?? Wait JP loop back to 0x208. Let me just write clean bytes and verify each 2-byte pair.

Clean demo (addresses):
0x200: 60 0A  LD V0, 0x0A
0x202: 61 0A  LD V1, 0x0A
0x204: 62 01  LD V2, 0x01
0x206: A2 20  LD I, 0x220
0x208: E0 95  SKP V5      ; if key 5 pressed → skip to 0x20C
0x20A: 12 0E  JP 0x20E    ; (not pressed) jump to move
0x20C: 62 FF  LD V2, 0xFF ; reverse dir
0x20E: 80 22  ADD V0, V2
0x210: D0 04  DRW V0, V1, 4
0x212: 12 08  JP 0x208    ; loop
0x214-0x217: sprite? No — sprite must be at 0x220 (I=0x220).
0x220: 33 33 00 00  sprite (2x2 square: rows 0x33, 0x33)

Wait, SKP V5 with V5 unset: SKP Vx skips if key V[x] is pressed. V5 is undefined (0) → key 0 is tested! Bug: I need V5 to hold 5. Add at init: 0x204: 65 05 (LD V5, 0x05). Let me redo:
0x200: 60 0A  LD V0, 0x0A
0x202: 61 0A  LD V1, 0x0A
0x204: 62 01  LD V2, 0x01
0x206: 65 05  LD V5, 0x05
0x208: A2 20  LD I, 0x220
0x20A: E0 95  SKP V5  → if pressed skip to 0x20E
0x20C: 12 10  JP 0x210    ; not pressed → move
0x20E: 62 FF  LD V2, 0xFF ; pressed → reverse
0x210: 80 22  ADD V0, V2
0x212: D0 04  DRW V0, V1, 4
0x214: 12 0A  JP 0x20A    ; loop
0x220: 33 33 00 00

That's correct. Also ADD V0,V2: 0x0A + 0xFF = 0x109 → V0 = 0x09, VF=1. Fine, wraps via &0xFF.

Also the demo currently loaded is DEMO_FINAL (buggy). Replace with the clean one.

9. decode() switch: case 0x0000 has `else if ((ins & 0x00F0) === 0x00AN)` — SyntaxError. Fix to 0x00A0. Also the SYS check `(ins & 0x00F0) === 0x00D0` — SYS is 0x00D0-0x00DF, mask 0x00F0 = 0x00D0. OK.
10. decode 8NN7: fix quote typo.
11. Also `const nnnn = ins & 0x0FFF;` unused, fine. `const xx` unused, fine.
12. step(): case 0xF000 0x18: `CHIP8.I = CHIP8.V[x]` — should be I = V[x] (address). Correct per spec (F18x LD I, Vx). OK.
13. F00A blocking wait — in a non-blocking emulator it just polls once; acceptable.
14. render(): img data — fine.
15. The leftover DEMO_ROM, DEMO_ROM_FIXED, DEMO constants are dead code — harmless but ugly. I'll remove them when replacing DEMO_FINAL.

Let me apply fixes with code_editing."}
